extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the clean verdict by testing whether the case exhibits the in-scope issue in either direction. First, denominator substitution: the code and the selected result both use the full planned count of 48, verified against the CSV (48 staged rows), so no retained-subset denominator stands in for the complete domain — 9/48 = 0.1875 is arithmetically correct as stated. Second, I tested whether restricting event counting to the 36 retained boxes silently converts a retained-subset statistic into a complete-domain claim: the interpretation-limits section explicitly discloses that the 12 removed boxes were never assessed, are non-events by construction, and that the figure is only a lower bound on the complete-planned-set rate, so the report does not assert a retained-subset estimate as the complete-domain occurrence rate. I could not construct a reading of the visible files in which the selected result attributes a subset-only statistic to the complete domain without qualification.
